findings.failure_mode: Missing file, permission error, or oversized file aborts the entire program instead of returning a typed error
findings.fix: Return Result<Vec<Record>, LoadError> and map io::Error to a typed error variant

findings.failure_mode: A line with non-numeric second field or missing comma causes a panic rather than a typed parse error
findings.fix: Use split_once(',') and map_err on parse to return a typed ParseError or LoadError variant

findings.problem: Lossy as<u16> conversion: parse::<u32>().unwrap() as u16 silently truncates values > 65535
findings.failure_mode: A valid u32 in range 65536..=4294967295 wraps to a wrong u16 value with no error, corrupting domain data
findings.fix: Use try_from::<u32, u16>() or explicit range check, returning an Overflow error variant on out-of-range values

findings.problem: Unbounded collect of split parts into Vec<String> with no domain cap on parts or line count
findings.failure_mode: A single line with millions of comma-separated fields or a file with millions of lines OOM-crashes the process
findings.fix: Validate line count against a MAX_LINES cap before the loop. For per-line parts, use split_once(',') and reject lines with more than the expected field count. Avoid collecting all parts into Vec.

findings.problem: println!("loaded {}", parts[0]) fuses stdout I/O into what should be a pure parser
findings.failure_mode: The parsing function has a side effect that cannot be tested deterministically, breaks functional-core isolation, and makes the function order-dependent (I/O interleaved with data construction)
findings.fix: Remove println! from the parser. If logging is needed, return a separate diagnostic/warning type or let the shell layer log after parsing completes

findings.problem: parts[0] and parts[1] are unchecked index accesses into a Vec created from split
findings.failure_mode: A line with zero commas (no separator) produces a single-element Vec; parts[1] panics at runtime. A line with only a comma produces an empty second element that parses to a parse error, compounding failures.
findings.fix: Use line.split_once(',') to get exactly two Option<&str> results. Handle None for the separator as a typed error instead of panicking.

findings.problem: load_shards returns Vec<Record> with no Result type, hiding all failure modes
findings.failure_mode: Callers cannot distinguish file-not-found, parse errors, type errors, or allocation failures. The API contract promises success or process termination.
findings.fix: Define a LoadError enum with FileIo, Parse, Overflow, and MalformedLine variants. Change signature to load_shards(path: &str) -> Result<Vec<Record>, LoadError>

findings.problem: Record.value is a bare u16 with no domain constraint enforcement at the type level
findings.failure_mode: Any code can construct Record { name, value: 0 } or Record { name, value: 65535 } with no indication whether those values are valid in the domain
findings.fix: Use a newtype BoundedValue(u16) with a smart constructor that validates the acceptable range, or encode value constraints directly in the Record constructor

findings.problem: load_shards performs file I/O (fs::read_to_string) and stdout I/O (println!) inside the same function that parses data
findings.failure_mode: The pure parsing logic cannot be unit-tested in isolation. The shell and core are fused, violating the Functional Core / Imperative Shell architecture. Side effects are not localized to a single boundary layer.
findings.fix: Split into: (1) parse_records(text: &str) -> Result<Vec<Record>, ParseError> as pure core, and (2) load_shards(path: &str) -> Result<Vec<Record>, LoadError> as shell that reads the file, calls parse_records, and handles I/O errors

findings.problem: text.lines() iterates the entire file eagerly with no progress limit or streaming
findings.failure_mode: A multi-gigabyte file loads fully into memory via read_to_string before any record is produced, causing OOM on hostile input
findings.fix: Use BufRead::BufReader with lines() iterator to stream the file. Add a MAX_LINES domain cap and return an error if exceeded

findings.problem: No try_reserve or capacity pre-allocation strategy; collect grows Vec with repeated reallocations
findings.failure_mode: For large but valid inputs, repeated Vec reallocations double the peak memory usage and add unpredictable latency to the hot path
findings.fix: If a line count cap is available, try_reserve that count. Otherwise accept the allocation cost but document it and add a benchmark for large-input performance

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists for load_shards throughput on typical shard sizes
no profiler evidence for allocation profile of parse path
no allocation budget or hot-path analysis for load_shards
no second-ring evidence for any performance or zero-cost claims (none are stated, but absence is notable for a data-loading function)
no command evidence: cargo fmt --check, cargo check, cargo clippy, and cargo test were not run
no test files exist to verify parsing behavior on malformed input, boundary values, or empty files
residual_risk: The crate has pervasive BLOCKER violations: forbidden constructs (unwrap, panic via indexing), no typed errors, hidden I/O in the core, unbounded resource consumption, lossy type conversions, and no tests or benchmarks. Every hostile input path leads to panic or data corruption. This code must be fully repaired before any delivery gate can pass.
